key_impacts: Severe social, economic and psychological impacts.
evidence_snippets: 17 January 1995: a magnitude 7.9 earthquake shook Kobe and adjoining areas in Hyogo Prefecture, Japan.
It took more than 6,400 lives, destroyed thousands of houses and left millions of people homeless.
2005 marks the 10th anniversary of the Great Hanshin-Awaji Earthquake of Kobe (Hyogo).
missing_information: Exact list of affected municipalities beyond Kobe.
Precise count of houses destroyed and total economic losses.

evidence_snippets: The impact of these lessons was visible in last year's Niigata Earthquake.
With a 6.8 magnitude, this earthquake generated similar intensity as the Kobe earthquake.
Building damages in Niigata were high; the human toll—35 lives lost—was far less severe.
missing_information: Numbers of injured, displaced, and economic losses.
